# Common networking surface area

Scope: the behavior that every network driver must have, and the Engine API requests for networks
and endpoints that do not depend on the network's driver. This spec describes them as observable
from outside the daemon.

This spec is a stub. It holds expectations that every network driver shares. They come from the work
on the other specs and from reviews of the specs' coverage. It is not yet a complete account.
[../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a spec, their
categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the conventions of the
networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence ceilings, and host
requirements. [Swarm networking surface area](swarm-networking.md) and [bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md) cover what
is specific to their drivers. [container-dns.md](container-dns.md) covers name resolution.

In this spec, a predefined network is a network that `GET /networks` with the filter
`type=builtin` lists. The expectations here also hold for Swarm-scoped networks and on
nodes in a Swarm, unless an expectation narrows them.
[Network lifecycle & API surface](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface) covers the requests that are specific to
Swarm-scoped networks. Where an expectation of swarm-networking.md says something different about
the same request or state, that expectation holds.

<a id="network-common-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-NET-REPEAT-CONNECT-STATUS-BY-SCOPE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-REPEAT-CONNECT-STATUS-BY-SCOPE**: Why a change to NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES should be deliberate

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES)

It catches a change that makes a repeat connect respond with one status on every network, in
place of 403 on a network that is not Swarm-scoped and 409 on an attachable Swarm-scoped
network; clients branch on either status, so the change should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-GWBRIDGE-NOT-PREDEFINED"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-GWBRIDGE-NOT-PREDEFINED**: Why a change to NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED should be deliberate

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED](#NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED)

It catches a change that makes network prune keep docker_gwbridge on a node that is not in a
Swarm; that would make it a system network that the documentation does not list, and an operator
would then have to remove a gateway network that they created by hand, so the change should be
deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING**: Why a change to NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING should be deliberate

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING](#NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING)

It catches a change of the status for a ConfigFrom that names a missing network, such as from
404 to 400; clients branch on 404 to tell a missing dependency from a malformed request, so the
change should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER**: Why a change to NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER should be deliberate

*Rationale of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER](#NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER)

It catches a change in how requested and generated interface names are assigned, such as
reserving the requested names before the others are generated; that decides which containers
start, so the change should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS**: Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests

*Rationale of:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

Expectations in several specs are scoped by a property of the network's driver, such as "a
driver that adds an interface to the container" or "a driver that accepts an endpoint MAC
address", and do not list the drivers. [*NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE*](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE) and
[*NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC*](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC) say which built-in drivers have each property. A driver that
started or stopped adding an interface would add or remove an interface in every container on
its networks, so the operator's tooling and debugging inside the container would see a different
set of interfaces. A driver that started or stopped accepting an endpoint MAC address would
change which requests that set `MacAddress` for an endpoint on its networks succeed.
Either change should be deliberate.

<a id="network-common-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

The kernel facilities are requirements of each Linux node. The host configuration is a requirement
of each node. The conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements).
The specs of the drivers list what each driver needs: [Host requirements](bridge-networking.md#bridge-networking-host-requirements),
[Host requirements](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-host-requirements) and [Host requirements](ipvlan-networking.md#ipvlan-networking-host-requirements).

<a id="NET-HOST-MACVLAN"></a>

**Host requirement NET-HOST-MACVLAN**: macvlan links

*Platforms:* linux · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `MACVLAN` · *Tags:* macvlan

*Pinned by:* [NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN](#NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN)

*Needed when:* A `macvlan` network

<a id="NET-HOST-DUMMY"></a>

**Host requirement NET-HOST-DUMMY**: Dummy links

*Platforms:* linux · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `DUMMY` · *Tags:* macvlan, no-parent

*Needed when:* A `macvlan` network without a `parent`

Not pinned. The error for a missing dummy link does not name the facility.

<a id="NET-HOST-VLAN"></a>

**Host requirement NET-HOST-VLAN**: VLAN links

*Platforms:* linux · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `VLAN_8021Q` · *Tags:* macvlan, vlan-parent

*Pinned by:* [NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN](#NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN)

*Needed when:* A `macvlan` network with a `parent` of the form
`<interface>.<VLAN ID>`

<a id="network-common-host-configuration"></a>

### Host configuration

<a id="NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC"></a>

daemon programs are not part of the host's firewall.

*Needed when:* Always, except in an expectation whose state names firewalld

<a id="needextend-network-network-common-1"></a>

<a id="network-common-network-api"></a>

## Network API

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME**: Creating a network with an existing network's name responds 409

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* An existing network that is not Swarm-scoped and not predefined

`POST /networks/create` with the network's name responds 409. `GET /networks`
then lists only one network with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI**: docker network create with an existing network's name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* An existing network that is not Swarm-scoped and not predefined

`docker network create` with the network's name exits non-zero and prints the daemon's
error. `docker network ls` then lists only one network with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME**: Outside a Swarm, a predefined or reserved network name responds 403

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node that is not in a Swarm

`POST /networks/create` with the name of a predefined network, `default` or
`container` responds 403. `POST /networks/create` with a name that starts with
`container:` also responds 403. `GET /networks` then does not list a new network with
that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER**: On a manager, the names bridge and host respond 409, the rest 403

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux manager

`POST /networks/create` with the name `bridge` or `host` responds 409.
It responds 403 when the name is `none`, `default` or `container`, or starts with
`container:`. This holds for the default driver and for `overlay`.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI**: docker network create with a predefined network's name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker network create` with the name of a predefined network exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED**: Deleting a predefined network responds 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for a predefined network responds 403. `GET /networks`
then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI**: docker network rm of a predefined network fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker network rm` for a predefined network exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error.
`docker network ls` then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403**: Deleting a network with a running container responds 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, with a running container attached to it

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 403. `GET /networks` then still
lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI**: docker network rm of a network with a running container fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, with a running container attached to it

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds with a 4xx or

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS**: Starting a container connected to a missing network responds 404

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, with a created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an `{id}` that is not the name
or an ID prefix of any network, responds 200. `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the
container then responds 404 while no network has that name. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER**: A container connected to a missing network uses it once it is created

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an `{id}` that is not the name
or an ID prefix of any network, responds 200. A network with that name is then created.
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds 204, and the container has
an address on that network. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, and a container that is not attached to it

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` that is
outside every subnet of that network responds 400, and does not create a container.
`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with that address,
responds 400, and does not attach the container.

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` for the
network `bridge` responds 400, and does not create a container. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to the network `bridge`, for the container, with a static
address in `IPAMConfig`, responds 400, and does not attach the container.

`docker run` and `docker network connect` with `--ip` outside every subnet

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with

`GET /networks/{id}` responds 200 with the network when `{id}` is the network's full

`docker network inspect` prints the network when it is given the network's full ID or its

`POST /networks/prune` does not delete `docker_gwbridge`. `GET /networks/docker_gwbridge` lists `ingress-sbox` in `Containers`.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CREATE"></a>

configuration. [*SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED*](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED) and
[*SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-UNATTACHED*](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-UNATTACHED) cover a Swarm-scoped network.

The network's containers get addresses in the subnets of the config-only network's
`IPAM` configuration.

`docker network create --config-from` naming a network that does not exist exits non-zero
and prints the daemon's error.

*Applies to:* A config-only network, and a network that is not Swarm-scoped whose
`ConfigFrom` names it

`docker network rm` for the config-only network exits non-zero and prints the daemon's
error.

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CTR-CREATE**: Creating a container on a config-only network responds 201

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /containers/create` for a container on that network responds 201. See

it

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds 200. See

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START**: A container on a config-only network does not start

*Applies to:* A created container on a config-only network

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status. The
container stays in the created state.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-HTTP403**: Starting a container on a config-only network responds 403

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 403. The container stays in the
created state. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-CLI**: docker run -d on a config-only network fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A config-only network

`docker run -d --network` naming that network exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING**: Connecting a running container to a config-only network fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a config-only network

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds with a 4xx or
5xx status. `GET /networks/{id}` then does not list the container.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-HTTP403**: A running container's connect to a config-only network responds 403

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a config-only network

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds 403, with a
message that contains `cannot create endpoint on configuration-only network`.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-LISTED"></a>

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a config-only network

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, fails,
`GET /containers/{id}/json` lists the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`.

*Applies to:* A running container, and a config-only network

`docker network connect` naming that network and the container exits non-zero and prints
the daemon's error.

<a id="network-common-endpoint-interfaces"></a>

## Endpoint interfaces

The expectations in this section hold for an endpoint of any network driver that adds an interface
to the container ([Driver properties](#network-common-driver-properties)). An endpoint requests an interface name
when its `com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` is set to that name.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED**: An endpoint's interface has the name that it requests

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* An endpoint that requests an interface name

The interface has that name. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT**: An interface without a requested name is named eth\<N>

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with an endpoint that does not request an interface name, on a network
of a built-in driver without `com.docker.network.container_iface_prefix`

The interface name is `eth<N>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START**: A container whose requested interface name is refused does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` the OS refuses

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT**: A connect whose requested interface name is refused fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` the OS refuses, responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500**: Starting with a refused interface name responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` the OS refuses

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `error renaming interface` and the requested name. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500**: A connect with a refused interface name responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` the OS refuses, responds 500. The message contains
`error renaming interface` and the requested name. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI**: docker run -d with a refused interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run -d` with a `com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses
exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect with a refused interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`docker network connect` for the container, with a
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses, exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CREATE**: A container requesting a duplicate interface name or lo is created

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

At API version 1.44 or later, `POST /containers/create` for a container with two
endpoints that request the same interface name responds 201. So does a request for a container
with an endpoint that requests `lo`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START**: A container whose endpoints request the same name does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with two endpoints that request
the same interface name

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-LO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-LO**: A container with an endpoint that requests lo does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with an endpoint that requests
`lo`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT**: A connect requesting lo or an existing interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint that requests
`lo`, responds with a 4xx or 5xx status. It does the same with an endpoint that requests
the name of one of the container's interfaces.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500**: A duplicate interface name or lo at start responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with two endpoints that request
the same interface name, or with one that requests `lo`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that names
the interface. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500**: A connect requesting lo or an existing name responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint that requests
`lo` or the name of one of its interfaces, responds 500. The message names the
interface. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI**: docker run -d with a duplicate interface name or lo fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run -d` exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error when two of the container's
endpoints request the same interface name. It does the same when an endpoint requests
`lo`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect requesting lo or an existing name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`docker network connect` for the container exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error
when the endpoint requests `lo` or the name of one of its interfaces.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS**: A standalone container's interface has its requested static address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running standalone container whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv4Address` or `IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`

Its interface on that network has that address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT**: A requested static address is reported in the container's settings

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running standalone container whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv4Address` or `IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`

`GET /containers/{id}/json` reports the address as `IPAddress` or
`GlobalIPv6Address` in `NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE**: An endpoint MacAddress set at create is the interface's MAC address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container created at API version 1.44 or later with an endpoint
`MacAddress` on a network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address

Its interface on that network has that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT**: An endpoint MacAddress set at connect is the interface's MAC address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` with `MacAddress` set, at API version
1.54 or later, responds 200, the container's interface on the network has that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT**: A connect with MacAddress fails where the driver does not accept it

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC
address

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with
`MacAddress` set, at API version 1.54 or later, responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.
`GET /networks/{id}` then does not list the container.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START**: A container with a MacAddress its driver refuses is created, not started

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC address
([Driver properties](#network-common-driver-properties))

At API version 1.44 or later, `POST /containers/create` for a container whose endpoint
on that network sets `MacAddress` responds 201. `POST /containers/{id}/start`
for the container then responds with a 4xx or 5xx status, and the container stays in the created
state.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI**: docker run -d with --mac-address fails where the driver refuses it

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

`docker run -d` with `--mac-address` and with `--network` naming a
network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC address exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN**: Without macvlan links, starting a macvlan container responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux host whose kernel does not offer macvlan links, and a created or stopped
container with an endpoint on a `macvlan` network

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `failed to create the macvlan port`. See [Host requirements](#network-common-host-requirements).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN**: Without VLAN links, a macvlan network on a VLAN parent responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux host whose kernel does not offer VLAN links

`POST /networks/create` for a `macvlan` network whose `parent` is
`<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, for an existing interface `<interface>` that does not yet have that
VLAN sub-interface, responds 500, with a message that contains `vlan link`. See
[Host requirements](#network-common-host-requirements).

<a id="network-common-default-gateway"></a>

## Default gateway

<a id="NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY**: A container on internal networks only has no default route

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container attached only to `internal` networks

The container does not have a default route. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-PRIORITY**: The default route goes through the endpoint with the highest GwPriority

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with endpoints on two or more networks that are not
`internal`, one with a higher `GwPriority` than the others

For each IP version that the endpoint gives the container a gateway or default route for, the
container's default route goes through that endpoint.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE**: With equal GwPriority, the default route follows a fixed endpoint order

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with endpoints on two or more networks that are not
`internal`, all with the same `GwPriority`

For each IP version, the container's default route is through the first endpoint that gives a
gateway or default route for that version, in this order: (1) endpoints that give one for both
IPv4 and IPv6, then endpoints that give one for a single version; (2) within each group, network
names in byte order.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE**: At API version 1.47 or earlier, container create ignores GwPriority

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

At API version 1.47 or earlier, `POST /containers/create` ignores
`GwPriority` in `EndpointsConfig`.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT**: A connect applies GwPriority at every API version

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` applies `GwPriority` at every API version.

<a id="network-common-file-etc-hosts"></a>

## `/etc/hosts`

This section holds on Linux nodes.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES**: /etc/hosts maps each of the container's addresses to its hostname

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container that does not use the host's network

For each of the container's addresses, `/etc/hosts` has a line that maps the address to
the container's hostname. The exceptions are addresses on the ingress network and on
`docker_gwbridge`. IPv6 addresses are also exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the
container, so that its loopback interface does not have an IPv6 address, for example with
`net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6` set to 1.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME**: A dotted hostname or a domain gives full and short names in /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose `Hostname` contains a dot, or that has a
`Domainname`

Each line for the container's addresses gives two names. The first is the full name: the
hostname, then a dot and the domain name if the container has one. The second is the part of the
hostname before its first dot.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-CONNECT**: A connect adds the container's addresses on the network to /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container responds 200, `/etc/hosts`
has the lines for the container's addresses on that network.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT**: A disconnect removes the network's addresses from /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a network, from its start or from a later
connect

After `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container responds 200,
`/etc/hosts` does not have the lines for the container's addresses on that network.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY**: A host-gateway entry maps to each address in host-gateway-ips

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with `host-gateway-ips` set

An entry `<name>:host-gateway` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts` adds a line to
`/etc/hosts` for each address in `host-gateway-ips`. Each line maps the
address to `<name>`.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: Without host-gateway-ips, host-gateway is the default bridge's gateways

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon without `host-gateway-ips`

An entry `<name>:host-gateway` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts` adds a line to
`/etc/hosts` for each gateway address of the default bridge. This holds whatever networks
the container is attached to.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE**: Without a host-gateway address, starting the container responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon without `host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to
`none`, and a created container with an entry `<name>:host-gateway` in
`HostConfig.ExtraHosts`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `unable to derive the IP value for host-gateway`. The container stays in the
created state. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#network-common-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI**: docker run with --add-host \<name>:host-gateway and no address fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon without `host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to
`none`

`docker run` with `--add-host` `<name>:host-gateway` exits non-zero and prints
the daemon's error.

<a id="network-common-driver-properties"></a>

## Driver properties

Expectations in this spec name a property of a network driver, not the driver itself, where the set
of drivers with the property can change. The two detectors below give the properties of the built-in
drivers. A plugin driver has the properties that it implements. The `l2tunnel` and
`ics` drivers have them on platforms that can create those networks.

<a id="NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE**: Which built-in drivers add an interface to the container

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumed by:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE) · *Rationale:* Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests ([RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS](#RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS))

A container on a network of one of these drivers has an interface on the network:

- `bridge`
- `overlay`
- `macvlan`
- `ipvlan`
- Windows: `nat`, `transparent`, `l2bridge`, `l2tunnel`,
  `ics`

A container on a network of one of these drivers does not:

- `host`
- `null` (the `none` network)

<a id="NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC**: Which built-in drivers accept an endpoint MAC address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumed by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-LISTED](#NET-API-CONNECT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-LISTED), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI) · *Rationale:* Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests ([RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS](#RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS))

These drivers accept an endpoint MAC address:

- `bridge`
- `overlay`
- `macvlan`
- Windows: `nat`, `transparent`, `l2bridge`, `l2tunnel`,
  `ics`

These drivers do not accept one:

- `ipvlan`

For these drivers, the property does not apply, because they add no interface:

- `host`
- `null` (the `none` network)

<a id="network-common-daemon-restart"></a>

## Daemon restart

<a id="NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED**: After SIGKILL and restart, the daemon's old namespaces are removed

*Observed from:* node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

After `SIGKILL` and restart, every network namespace that the daemon created before the
kill is removed, other than an overlay network's namespace and the namespace of a container that
live-restore keeps running. This includes the namespaces of load-balancer and ingress sandboxes,
and of containers that the daemon does not keep running. An overlay network's namespace is the
one that holds the network's VXLAN device. A namespace that the daemon creates after the restart
is a different namespace, even at the same path. The expectation is checked as soon as the
daemon's API answers again, without a ceiling, on a node in a Swarm too. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE**: With live-restore, a container keeps its namespace and interfaces

*Observed from:* node, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container, whose daemon has `live-restore`
true

After `SIGKILL` and restart, the container keeps its network namespace and its
interfaces.

<a id="network-common-known-divergences-non-goals"></a>

## Known divergences & non-goals

<a id="NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED**: HTTP 500 for refused requests

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Each request below is refused on purpose, but it responds 500. 500 is the status for a fault in
the daemon. The requests are: (1) `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for a container that
is not attached to the network. (2) `POST /containers/{id}/start` and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for an endpoint with a `com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that
the OS refuses, or that another endpoint of the container already uses. (3) `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container with a `host-gateway` entry in
`HostConfig.ExtraHosts`, when the daemon does not have an address for
`host-gateway`. (4) On a node in a Swarm, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created
or stopped container that `POST /networks/{id}/connect` connected to a network that does
not exist ([Network API](#network-common-network-api), [Swarm-scoped networks](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks),
[Endpoint interfaces](#network-common-endpoint-interfaces), [/etc/hosts](#network-common-file-etc-hosts)).

<a id="NET-API-STOPPED-CTR-UNUSABLE-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-STOPPED-CTR-UNUSABLE-NETWORK**: Networks that a created or stopped container cannot use

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Accepted. For a created or stopped container, `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a network
that does not exist, or to a config-only network, responds 200. `POST /containers/create` for a container on a config-only network also responds 201. Only
`POST /containers/{id}/start` refuses the network. For a network that does not exist, it
responds 404 with `network <name> not found` on a node that is not in a Swarm. On a
node in a Swarm, it responds 500 with a message that contains `network <name> not found`. For a config-only network, it responds 403 with `cannot create endpoint on configuration-only network`. If a network with the missing name is created before the start, the
start attaches the container to it ([Network API](#network-common-network-api)).

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES**: Connecting a running container to a network it is already attached to

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* Why a change to NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-TWO-STATUSES should be deliberate ([RAT-NET-REPEAT-CONNECT-STATUS-BY-SCOPE](#RAT-NET-REPEAT-CONNECT-STATUS-BY-SCOPE))

Refused with two different statuses. The request responds 403 on a network that is not
Swarm-scoped, and 409 on an attachable Swarm-scoped network ([Network API](#network-common-network-api),
[Swarm-scoped networks](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING**: HTTP 404 for a missing ConfigFrom network

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* Why a change to NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING should be deliberate ([RAT-NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING](#RAT-NET-API-HTTP404-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING))

`POST /networks/create` with `ConfigFrom` naming a network that does not
exist responds 404. 404 is the status for a request whose own resource does not exist. Here the
request is valid, and its body names the missing network ([Network API](#network-common-network-api)).

<a id="NET-FILTER-TYPE-SEVERAL-VALUES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-FILTER-TYPE-SEVERAL-VALUES**: Several values for the type filter

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Not combined. With both `type=builtin` and `type=custom` given,
`GET /networks` tests each network against one of the two values, chosen at random. The
response lists a different subset of the networks each time. As with other filter terms, a
network is meant to match when it matches either value ([Network API](#network-common-network-api)).

<a id="NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE**: Default route on internal overlays on Windows

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* windows

A Windows container attached only to `internal` overlays has a default route
([Default gateway](#network-common-default-gateway)).

<a id="NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED**: ifname option on Windows

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

Ignored. A Windows container's interface name does not follow
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` ([Endpoint interfaces](#network-common-endpoint-interfaces)).

<a id="NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT**: Interface left behind after a failed connect

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

If `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container fails at the rename, the
interface stays in the container under its generated `veth` name. The interface is
down and does not have addresses. Its host-side peer stays attached. The interface and the peer
stay until the container's network namespace is destroyed. A failed connect is meant to leave
nothing in place ([Endpoint interfaces](#network-common-endpoint-interfaces)).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE**: Interface names the kernel rewrites

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Accepted without an error. For a name that contains `%d`, the kernel gives the interface the
first free name that matches, such as `eth0`. A later disconnect responds 200, but the
interface stays in the container. The interface stays up and keeps its address
([Endpoint interfaces](#network-common-endpoint-interfaces)).

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER**: Interface-name collisions depend on attach order

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* Why a change to NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER should be deliberate ([RAT-NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER](#RAT-NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER))

Take a container with two endpoints. One endpoint asks for `eth0`. The name of the other
endpoint is generated. The container starts or fails, depending on the order in which its
endpoints are attached. This order is random. The endpoint that asks for the name is meant to
get it, whatever the order ([Endpoint interfaces](#network-common-endpoint-interfaces)).

<a id="NET-FAILED-CONNECT-NETWORK-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-FAILED-CONNECT-NETWORK-LISTED**: Network listed after a failed connect

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Left in place. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container can fail when the
daemon creates the endpoint. For example, it fails when the network's driver does not accept the
endpoint, or when the network is config-only. After such a failure, `GET /containers/{id}/json` lists the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`, but the
container does not have an endpoint on it. A failed connect is meant to leave nothing in place
([Network API](#network-common-network-api)).

<a id="NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED**: docker_gwbridge outside a Swarm

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* Why a change to NET-API-GWBRIDGE-PRUNED should be deliberate ([RAT-NET-GWBRIDGE-NOT-PREDEFINED](#RAT-NET-GWBRIDGE-NOT-PREDEFINED))

Pruned. On a node that is not in a Swarm, `docker_gwbridge` is not a predefined
network. `POST /networks/prune` deletes it while no running container is attached to it.
This includes a `docker_gwbridge` that an operator creates before the node joins a
Swarm, to configure the gateway network ([Network API](#network-common-network-api),
[Gateway network](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-gateway-network)).

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED**: dangling filter for Swarm-scoped networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Wrong. On a manager, `GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=true` lists
every Swarm-scoped network, in use or not. A Swarm-scoped network with a local attachment is
listed for `dangling=false` too. A network that services or containers use is meant
to be listed only for `dangling=false`
([Swarm-scoped networks](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX**: Names that are a prefix of a Swarm-scoped network's ID

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Resolved to the Swarm-scoped network on a manager. On a manager, `GET /networks/{id}`
and `docker network inspect` with the name of a network that is not Swarm-scoped return a
Swarm-scoped network whose ID starts with that name. On other nodes, and for networks that are
not Swarm-scoped, a full-name match takes precedence over a partial ID
([Swarm-scoped networks](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks), [Network API](#network-common-network-api)).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED**: Aliases in a service's Hosts

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Dropped. `ContainerSpec.Hosts` takes entries in the form `<address> <name> <alias>...`, as in hosts(5). A task's `/etc/hosts` has a line that maps `<address>` to
`<name>` only. The aliases are meant to map to `<address>` too
([/etc/hosts](#network-common-file-etc-hosts)).
